question.worked_solution:
We start with the ratio $4:1$ and write it as a fraction:

$$
\frac{4}{1}
$$

So the numerator represents the left-hand entry ($4$), and the denominator represents the right-hand entry ($1$).

We can generate equivalent ratios by finding equivalent fractions:

- To create a numerator of $16,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator of our fraction by $4:$

$$
\frac{4\times 4}{1\times 4}=\frac{16}{4}
$$

- To create a numerator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator of our fraction by $5:$

$$
\frac{4\times 5}{1\times 5}=\frac{20}{5}
$$

- To create a numerator of $28,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator of our fraction by $7:$

$$
\frac{4\times 7}{1\times 7}=\frac{28}{7}
$$

Finally, we fill in the ratio table:

| $4$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- |
| $16$ | $4$ |
| $20$ | $5$ |
| $28$ | $7$ |

$$

$$
